dummies = []
for c in CATS:
    dm = pd.get_dummies(S[c], prefix=c, dtype=float)
    ref_col = f"{c}_{REF[c]}" if f"{c}_{REF[c]}" in dm else dm.columns[0]
    dummies.append(dm.drop(columns=ref_col))
XS = sm.add_constant(pd.concat([S[num_terms]] + dummies, axis=1))
GROUPS = {"budget (log + curve)": ["log_budget_c", "log_budget_sq"], "runtime": ["runtime_min"], "release month": ["release_month"],
          "sequel": ["sequel"], "major producer": ["major_producer"],
          "director track record": ["director_prior_films", "director_prior_hit_rate", "director_has_history"],
          "writer track record": ["writer_prior_films", "writer_prior_hit_rate", "writer_has_history"],
          "company track record": ["company_prior_films", "company_prior_hit_rate", "company_has_history"],
          "rating-overlap competition": ["rating_overlap_competition"]}
for c in CATS:
    GROUPS[{"mpaa_rating": "MPAA rating", "primary_genre": "primary genre", "origin_group": "origin (US / non-US)", "distributor_group": "distributor group",
            "release_weekday": "release weekday", "source_group": "source group", "original_language": "original language"}[c]] = [x for x in XS.columns if x.startswith(c + "_")]


def fit(cols):
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        return sm.Logit(yl, XS[cols]).fit(disp=0, maxiter=500, method="newton")


full = fit(list(XS.columns))
null_ll = sm.Logit(yl, XS[["const"]]).fit(disp=0).llf
print(f"Full model: {len(XS.columns) - 1} terms; log-likelihood {full.llf:.1f} (no-feature model {null_ll:.1f}); "
      f"McFadden pseudo-R² {1 - full.llf / null_ll:.3f}; AIC {full.aic:.1f}")

rows = []
for g, cols in GROUPS.items():
    red = fit([c for c in XS.columns if c not in cols])
    lr = 2 * (full.llf - red.llf); df = len(cols)
    from scipy.stats import chi2
    rows.append({"feature": g, "terms": df, "LR chi²": round(lr, 1), "p-value": chi2.sf(lr, df),
                 "AIC if removed (+ = worse)": round(red.aic - full.aic, 1),
                 "pseudo-R² lost": round((1 - full.llf / null_ll) - (1 - red.llf / null_ll), 4)})
fit_tab = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("feature").sort_values("LR chi²", ascending=False)
fit_tab["verdict"] = np.where((fit_tab["p-value"] < 0.05) & (fit_tab["AIC if removed (+ = worse)"] > 2), "keep",
                              np.where(fit_tab["p-value"] < 0.10, "borderline", "drop candidate"))
fit_tab["p-value"] = fit_tab["p-value"].map(lambda p: f"{p:.1e}" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}")
display(fit_tab)'''),
C('''coef = pd.DataFrame({"coef": full.params, "std err": full.bse, "z": full.tvalues, "p-value": full.pvalues, "odds ratio": np.exp(full.params)}).drop(index="const")
coef["p-value"] = coef["p-value"].map(lambda p: f"{p:.1e}" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}")
print("Coefficients (numbers standardized: odds ratio per 1 standard deviation; categories vs reference "

with pd.option_context("display.max_rows", 120):

C('''tree_models = {"Random forest": MODELS["Random forest"], "XGBoost": MODELS["XGBoost"]}
FEAT_COLS = {"budget (log + curve)": ["log_budget"], "runtime": ["runtime_min"], "release month": ["release_month"], "sequel": ["sequel"],
             "major producer": ["major_producer"], "director track record": ["director_prior_films", "director_prior_hit_rate", "director_has_history"],
             "writer track record": ["writer_prior_films", "writer_prior_hit_rate", "writer_has_history"],
             "company track record": ["company_prior_films", "company_prior_hit_rate", "company_has_history"],
             "rating-overlap competition": ["rating_overlap_competition"], "MPAA rating": ["mpaa_rating"], "primary genre": ["primary_genre"],
             "origin (US / non-US)": ["origin_group"], "distributor group": ["distributor_group"], "release weekday": ["release_weekday"],
             "source group": ["source_group"], "original language": ["original_language"]}
base_auc = {k: roc_auc_score(yl, OOF[k]) for k in tree_models}
agree = []
for g, cols in FEAT_COLS.items():
    r = {"feature": g}
    for k, mdl in tree_models.items():
        nums_k = [c for c in ["log_budget"] + NUMS if c not in cols]; cats_k = [c for c in CATS if c not in cols]
        pre = ColumnTransformer([("num", "passthrough", nums_k), ("cat", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", min_frequency=20, sparse_output=False), cats_k)])

    agree.append(r)
agree = pd.DataFrame(agree).set_index("feature").join(fit_tab[["LR chi²", "p-value", "AIC if removed (+ = worse)", "verdict"]])
display(agree.sort_values("LR chi²", ascending=False))'''),

| Model | In plain words |

for c in ["director", "writer", "company"]:

CATS = ["mpaa_rating", "primary_genre", "origin_group", "distributor_group", "release_weekday", "source_group", "original_language"]
NUMS = ["runtime_min", "release_month", "sequel", "major_producer", "director_prior_films", "director_prior_hit_rate", "director_has_history",
        "writer_prior_films", "writer_prior_hit_rate", "writer_has_history", "company_prior_films", "company_prior_hit_rate", "company_has_history",

- **Pseudo-R² (McFadden):** 1 − (log-likelihood of the model ÷ log-likelihood of a model with no features). For logistic regression, 0.2–0.4 is considered a good fit.
- **AIC:** fit penalized for the number of parameters; lower is better. A feature earns its place if removing it **raises** AIC by more than about 2.
- **Likelihood-ratio test:** refit without the feature (all its categories at once) and test whether the fit got significantly worse (χ², p < 0.05 = keep).

S = D.copy()

for c in CATS:

            "release_weekday": "release weekday", "source_group": "source group", "original_language": "original language"}[c]] = [x for x in XS.columns if x.startswith(c + "_")]


def fit(cols):
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        return sm.Logit(yl, XS[cols]).fit(disp=0, maxiter=500, method="newton")

rows = []

content.text:
So far we'd used one model: gradient-boosted trees (scikit-learn's `HistGradientBoostingClassifier`). I've now compared five model types and tested every feature's fit, in a new §19 of your notebook. Everything is cross-validated on the 2000–2015 films, and the test years are still locked.

**Model comparison** (same features, same folds)

| Model | AUC (95% range) | Winners caught in the top 20% | Hit rate in the top 20% |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logistic regression** | **0.766** (0.750–0.783) | 38.3% | 63% |
| XGBoost | 0.759 (0.741–0.774) | 38.0% | 63% |
| Gradient boosting | 0.758 | 37.2% | 62% |
| Random forest | 0.751 | 38.0% | 63% |
| Decision tree | 0.705 | 34.1% | 56% |
| Baseline | 0.609 | 28.0% | 46% |

The top four are statistically tied. **I'd use logistic regression as the main model:** it's as accurate as the others, its probabilities are the most reliable, and every feature can be explained and tested. XGBoost would be the challenger.

**Feature fit** (logistic regression on all 3,708 training films; pseudo-R² 0.20, AIC 3,878)
- **Keep (strong):** budget, distributor group, MPAA rating, company track record, sequel, primary genre, origin, runtime, source group, rating-overlap competition, release weekday. All pass the likelihood-ratio test (p < 0.005), AIC gets worse without each one, and the tree models mostly agree.
- **Borderline:** director track record (p = 0.035) and major producer (p = 0.013). They're significant in the regression, but the tree models lose nothing without them, because they overlap with company track record and distributor.
- **Drop:** release month (p = 0.67), writer track record (p = 0.54) and original language (p = 0.22). Removing each one *improves* AIC, and the trees don't use them.

**Two surprises in the coefficients**
- **Budget turns negative once everything else is accounted for.** Among films with the same distributor, rating and genre, cheaper ones more often clear 1.25×. Big budgets only look good on their own because they come with majors and sequels.
- **Runtime turns positive** for the same reason. Raw, long films looked bad because many are dramas.

**One more leak caught and checked:** the "blank" categories for source and origin mark losers perfectly, the same leak as the "was blank" flags. Merging them into ordinary categories barely changes accuracy (0.766 → 0.764), so the models weren't leaning on them. They should still be merged.

To get the statistics and XGBoost, I installed `statsmodels` and `xgboost` and pinned them in `requirements.txt`. Matt will need to reinstall the requirements.

Nothing is committed yet. Should I apply the drops and blank merges and refit, then commit?

message.content: First, help me understand the numbers here. Are these numbers precision and recall for the logistical regression? We beat the baseline by 10%, but what does that 10% mean? 38% still feels like a low number for a prediction model.

content.text:
Yes. They're **recall and precision**, measured at one cutoff: the model's top 20% of films.

| Measure | What it is | Logistic | Baseline | Random |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hit rate @20%** | **Precision:** of the films we pick, the share that are winners | 63% | 46% | 33% |
| **Winners caught @20%** | **Recall:** of all winners, the share we pick | 38% | 28% | 20% |
| **AUC** | Pick one winner and one loser at random: how often the model ranks the winner higher | 0.77 | 0.61 | 0.50 |

**The "+10 points" is recall:** the model finds 38% of all winners vs 28% for the baseline, about **37% more winners from the same number of picks**.

**Why 38% looks low:** we only pick 20% of films, but 33% of films are winners, so even a perfect model could catch at most 60% (20 ÷ 33). Recall is capped by how few we pick. I'm computing the full trade-off so you can see what happens at other cutoffs:

Yes. They're **recall and precision**, measured at one cutoff: the model's top 20% of films.

| Measure | What it is | Logistic | Baseline | Random |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hit rate @20%** | **Precision:** of the films we pick, the share that are winners | 63% | 46% | 33% |
| **Winners caught @20%** | **Recall:** of all winners, the share we pick | 38% | 28% | 20% |
| **AUC** | Pick one winner and one loser at random: how often the model ranks the winner higher | 0.77 | 0.61 | 0.50 |

**The "+10 points" is recall:** the model finds 38% of all winners vs 28% for the baseline, about **37% more winners from the same number of picks**.

**Why 38% looks low:** we only pick 20% of films, but 33% of films are winners, so even a perfect model could catch at most 60% (20 ÷ 33). Recall is capped by how few we pick. I'm computing the full trade-off so you can see what happens at other cutoffs:

input.description: Compute precision and recall at several pick cutoffs

content.text:
Here's the same model at different cutoffs, on the 3,708 training films (1,227 of them winners):

| Pick the top… | Films picked | Winners among them | Precision | Recall | Best possible recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10% | 371 | 268 | **72%** | 22% | 30% |
| **20%** (the contract) | 742 | 470 | **63%** | **38%** | 60% |
| 33% | 1,224 | 700 | 57% | 57% | 100% |
| 50% | 1,854 | 926 | 50% | 75% | 100% |

At 20%, the baseline picks 344 winners and the model picks **470, about 126 more from the same number of films**.

**How to read it:**
- **Recall is capped by how many you pick.** 38% at 20% is roughly two-thirds of the way to the 60% maximum. Pick half the films and recall goes to 75%.
- **Precision is the business number.** At a 33% base rate, a random pick is a winner one time in three. The model's picks are winners 63% of the time, and 72% if you only take its top 10%. The more selective you are, the more reliable each pick gets.
- **It's a trade-off, not a fixed score.** Picking more raises recall and lowers precision. The contract fixed 20% as the review capacity, which is why we quote that point.

**Is it good?** For predicting box office before release, an AUC of 0.77 is solid. Film success is famously hard to call ("nobody knows anything," as screenwriter William Goldman put it), and the model only sees what's known before release: no trailers, buzz or marketing spend. Being right two out of three times on its top picks, versus one in three by chance, is a real edge. It won't make 38% recall look like 90%, because that number is mostly limited by picking only 20%.

I applied the drops and blank merges and refit both models, in a new §20 of your notebook. It's still cross-validated on 2000–2015, with the test years locked.

**Results**

| Model | AUC (95% range) | Recall @20% | Precision @20% |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0.609 | 28.0% | 46% |
| **Logistic regression (refit)** | **0.767** (0.753–0.782) | **38.6%** | **64%** |
| XGBoost (refit) | 0.756 | 36.8% | 61% |

Logistic regression held steady (0.766 → 0.767) with 12 fewer terms, so the dropped features weren't helping. XGBoost dipped slightly, so logistic stays the main model.

**At other cutoffs** (logistic):

| Pick the top… | Precision | Recall |
|---|---|---|
| 10% | 73% | 22% |
| 20% | 64% | 39% |
| 33% | 57% | 57% |
| 50% | 51% | 76% |

**Fit check:** pseudo-R² is 0.193 (was 0.200) and AIC is 3,885 (was 3,878). Both got slightly worse, as expected: the merged blank categories had been "helping" the fit through the leak.

**New finding: source group stopped passing the test** (p = 0.39). Once the blanks were merged, comic vs book vs original added nothing beyond genre, rating and the rest. Its earlier signal was mostly the blank leak. It's the next drop candidate, though your adaptations-vs-originals point still holds as a description.

**Every other feature passes** (p < 0.01): budget, distributor, rating, company track record, sequel, genre, origin, runtime, rating-overlap competition, director track record, weekday and major producer. The odds ratios barely moved:
- **Rating:** G 2.3×, R 0.59×, NR 0.06× (vs PG-13)
- **Genre:** horror 2.6×, animation 2.0×, comedy 1.6× (vs drama)
- **Origin:** non-US 0.43×
- **Distributor:** specialty 0.32× (vs a major)
- **Other:** Wednesday release 1.48×; sequel 1.34× and company track record 1.33× per standard step

**The team write-up:** a separate agent is building a shareable page with the main comparison charts, the engineered features table and these model results, in plain language for people who won't run the notebook. I'll send you the link when it's ready.

Nothing is committed yet: §19–20, the new requirements and the earlier fit work. Should I drop source group too, then commit and push?

import nbformat
p='notebooks/Edwards-A10.ipynb'
nb=nbformat.read(p,4)
M=nbformat.v4.new_markdown_cell; C=nbformat.v4.new_code_cell
nb.cells.extend([
M('''### 20c. Drop source group too (Tanner, 2026-11-27)

After the blank merge, source group failed the likelihood-ratio test (p = 0.39) and removing it lowered AIC by 4.8: once genre, rating, sequel and the rest are known, comic vs book vs original adds nothing. Refit without it.'''),
C('''CATS3 = [c for c in CATS2 if c != "source_group"]
X3 = X2.drop(columns="source_group")
pre_lin3 = ColumnTransformer([
    ("budget", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), SplineTransformer(n_knots=5, degree=3)), ["log_budget"]),
    ("num", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), StandardScaler()), NUMS2),
    ("cat", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", min_frequency=20), CATS3)])
pre_tree3 = ColumnTransformer([("num", "passthrough", ["log_budget"] + NUMS2),
                               ("cat", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", min_frequency=20, sparse_output=False), CATS3)])
FINAL3 = {"Logistic regression": make_pipeline(pre_lin3, LogisticRegression(max_iter=3000, C=0.5)),
          "XGBoost": make_pipeline(pre_tree3, XGBClassifier(n_estimators=400, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8,
                                                            min_child_weight=5, reg_lambda=1.0, eval_metric="logloss", random_state=560, n_jobs=4))}
OOF3 = {name: cv_predict(m, X3) for name, m in FINAL3.items()}
rows = []
rng = np.random.default_rng(560)
for name, s in [("Baseline (b)", oof_b), ("Logistic (§20, with source group)", OOF2["Logistic regression"]),
                ("Logistic (final, no source group)", OOF3["Logistic regression"]), ("XGBoost (final, no source group)", OOF3["XGBoost"])]:
    b = [roc_auc_score(yl[i], s[i]) for i in (rng.integers(0, len(yl), len(yl)) for _ in range(300))]
    cap, prec = capture_at(s, yl)
    rows.append({"model": name, "AUC": round(roc_auc_score(yl, s), 3), "AUC 95% range": f"{np.percentile(b, 2.5):.3f}–{np.percentile(b, 97.5):.3f}",
                 "recall @20%": f"{cap:.1%}", "precision @20%": f"{prec:.1%}"})
display(pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("model"))
pr = []
for k in [0.10, 0.20, 0.33, 0.50]:
    n = int(round(k * len(yl))); top = np.argsort(-OOF3["Logistic regression"])[:n]; tp = int(yl[top].sum())
    pr.append({"pick top": f"{k:.0%}", "winners picked": tp, "of films picked": n, "precision": f"{tp / n:.0%}", "recall": f"{tp / yl.sum():.0%}"})
print("Final logistic model, precision and recall by pick size:")
display(pd.DataFrame(pr).set_index("pick top"))
cols3 = [c for c in XS2.columns if not c.startswith("source_group_")]
full3 = fit2(cols3)
print(f"Final logistic: {len(cols3) - 1} terms; McFadden pseudo-R² {1 - full3.llf / null_ll:.3f}; AIC {full3.aic:.1f} (with source group: {full2.aic:.1f})")
rows = []
for g, cols in G2.items():
    if g == "source group":
        continue
    red = fit2([c for c in cols3 if c not in cols]); lr = 2 * (full3.llf - red.llf)
    rows.append({"feature": g, "LR chi²": round(lr, 1), "p-value": chi2.sf(lr, len(cols)), "AIC if removed (+ = worse)": round(red.aic - full3.aic, 1)})
ft3 = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("feature").sort_values("LR chi²", ascending=False)
ft3["p-value"] = ft3["p-value"].map(lambda p: f"{p:.1e}" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}")
display(ft3)'''),
])
nbformat.write(nb,p)
EOF
